trajectory_summary: The call opens cooperatively through standard verification, then the customer delivers a detailed, informed cost objection (specific bill figures, payback-period math, prior solar experience) that the rep has no strong answer for. Within seconds of validating that objection, the rep pivots to the tree-shade issue and disqualifies the customer outright, ending the call in under three minutes with no design offer, no bill document ask, and no attempt to work the objection further.
outcome_dispute: Stage 3 is not disputing that this call ended as a DQ — it is disputing whether the DQ was procedurally sound. The shade/tree issue was real, but the rep never quantified actual shade impact (percentage of roof affected, time of day, panel placement options) before declaring solar unworkable, and the DQ was invoked immediately after the customer raised a cost objection the rep could not counter. The sequencing suggests the shade rationale may have been used opportunistically as an exit rather than a rigorously verified disqualifier.

observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep explicitly disqualifies the lead and ends the call with no appointment, next step, or bill collection — a clear DQ outcome, though its procedural soundness is contested in the trajectory verdict.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The call ended in a DQ before the rep reached bill-collection; the customer's bill figures were given verbally as part of his objection, not solicited as a document.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked what interested the customer in solar; the call moved directly from address/home-type verification into the shade concern before this section could be reached.

primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep validated the customer's low-bill objection at 02:02 and disqualified on shade twelve seconds later, with no quantification of the shade impact and no attempt to re-engage the customer's own 'I'm more willing to listen' opening at 01:53. Review whether this was a genuine technical DQ or an exit from a hard conversation the rep didn't have an answer for.

key_moments.quote: Now, Kevin, one thing I'm a little concerned about is you've got some trees that are putting some shade on the home.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the root of the whole disputed trajectory: the rep raises the shade concern unprompted and early, before any cost pushback has occurred, which supports the reading that it started as a genuine qualifying question rather than a manufactured exit. Its later use as an instant hard DQ right after the cost objection is what turns this from legitimate qualification into a questionable pattern.
